children.translated_text: I worship in my heart the one who pervades every particular form of the moving and unmoving, who consists of consciousness, is infinite, and has no beginning—
Lord <s>Bhairava</s>, refuge of the helpless—with my mind wholly absorbed in you.

children.text: tvanmayam etad aśeṣam idānīṃ bhāti mama tvadanugrahaśaktyā
children.translated_text: Through the power of your grace, all this now appears to me as consisting of you.

children.text: tvaṃ ca maheśa sadaiva mamātmā svātmamayaṃ mama tena samastam ||
children.translated_text: And you, O <s>Maheśa</s>, are always my own Self; therefore everything is made of my Self.

children.text: svātmani viśvagaye tvayi nāthe tena na saṃsṛṣṭibhītikathāsti
children.translated_text: Because, O Lord, the universe rests in you, who are present within the Self, there is no question of fear of transmigration,
even though hosts of karmic forces exist that cause terror through unbearable suffering and delusion.

children.text: antaka māṃ prati mā dṛśam enaṃ krodhakarālatamāṃ vinidhehi
children.translated_text: O <s>Antaka</s> (Death), do not direct toward me this gaze of yours, utterly dreadful with wrath.
Steadfast in the service and contemplation of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, I am filled with the power of the terrifying <s>Bhairava</s>.
Thus, with the vast darkness torn apart by the rays of consciousness strengthened through being filled with you,

children.text: mṛtyuyamāntakakarmapiśācair nātha namo 'stu na jātu bibhemi ||
children.translated_text: I am never afraid of death, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Antaka</s>, karma, or <s>piśācas</s> (demons). O Lord, homage to you!
Beholding the true nature of every object in the universe by the rays of true awakening that have arisen,

children.text: bhāvaparāmṛtanirbharapūrṇe tvayy aham ātmani nirvṛtim emi ||
children.translated_text: I attain repose in you, my Self, who are completely full of the supreme nectar of reality.
Whenever a state of affliction that causes bodily anguish enters the range of my mind,
O Lord, at that very moment a rain of supreme nectar from the hymn of my non-difference from you arises for me.
O <s>Śaṅkara</s>, this is the truth: this is the observance, gift, ablution, and austerity that destroys the anguish of worldly existence—
contemplation of the supreme nectar of your scripture, which pours a stream of repose into the mind.

children.text: nṛtyati gāyati hṛṣyati gāḍhaṃ saṃvid iyaṃ mama bhairavanātha
children.translated_text: This consciousness of mine dances, sings, and rejoices intensely, O Lord <s>Bhairava</s>,

children.text: tvāṃ priyam āpya sudarśanam ekam durlabham anyajanaiḥ samayajñam ||
children.translated_text: having attained you, the one beloved, beautiful to behold, difficult for other people to attain, and knower of the sacred tradition.

children.text: vasurasapauṣe kṛṣṇadaśamyām abhinavaguptaḥ stavam imam akarot
children.translated_text: In the year expressed by “Vasu-rasa,” on the tenth lunar day of the dark fortnight of <s>Pauṣa</s>, <s>Abhinavagupta</s> composed this hymn,

children.text: yena vibhur bhavamarusantāpaṃ śamayati janasya jhaṭiti dayāluḥ ||
children.translated_text: by which the merciful, all-pervading Lord swiftly calms for people the scorching heat of the desert of worldly existence.
This hymn called <s>Abhinava</s>, a set of nine verses, is complete.
